business_problem: TDHS needed to modernize how citizens applied for benefits and got support because separate service teams, lost data trails, and manual application checks slowed social-service delivery during emergencies and routine benefits processing alike.
solution_summary: TDHS built a citizen-facing support model on ServiceNow Customer Service Management so applications, status tracking, chatbot conversations, and casework could move through one customer record. The department first proved the platform by standing up emergency portals quickly for tornado and childcare-benefit programs, then expanded it into a broader constituent portal where Tennesseans can self-serve information, submit applications, and see case-specific dashboards from any device. Virtual Agent handles high-volume questions through the website, Facebook page, customer portal, and telephony integration, while preserving the conversation history when a live agent takes over. Behind the scenes, ServiceNow automates application-completeness checks, emails citizens if more information is needed, and routes ready cases to the correct worker. That shift turned benefits delivery from a fragmented, program-centric process into a customer-centric workflow with better continuity, faster triage, and much less backlog.

solution_components.name: Virtual Agent
solution_components.role: Handles FAQ-style interactions across digital channels and passes context to live agents when escalation is needed.

solution_components.name: Customer portal
solution_components.role: Lets constituents apply for benefits, track status, and access case-specific information through self-service.

data_flow: Citizens apply or ask questions through the portal, website, Facebook page, or telephony-linked Virtual Agent. ServiceNow keeps those interactions on one customer record, automates completeness checks on submitted applications, notifies citizens when more information is needed, and routes complete cases to workers who continue from the preserved conversation history.
business_outcome: TDHS stood up an essential-worker portal in three days, handles about 380K Virtual Agent chats a year, serves one-third of that volume outside business hours, delivers capacity equivalent to about 22 call-center agents, and moved case decisions from monthslong backlogs to a couple of days or at most two weeks.
